phase: Inc-2 DEPART per docs/FLIGHT_RELIABILITY_ROADMAP_2026-07-01.md §2-3; sibling B of the post-847ab19 pair (Max chose two siblings at scope 2026-07-15). Mechanism decisions from the roadmap's research conclusions: (1) DEPART's first act is a radial climb away from the current body, gated by v/vmax, THEN orbit-to-horizon alignment toward the next target — hand off to TRANSIT only once the nose clears the horizon (Elite escape-vector doctrine promoted from mitigation to first act). (2) Commit-and-hold phase discipline: once DEPART/TRANSIT/ARRIVE is chosen, hold that phase's control law to completion — no blended loops, no reactive re-optimization (the documented anti-patterns). (3) Arrival = ETA-scheduled deceleration culminating at the capture window (MechJeb/ED blue-zone pattern), replacing the HOLD position-lerp (SupercruisePilot HOLD easing — the 'tractor beam'); pilot-layer throttle policy ONLY, zero SC_TUNING contact. Carried-in residuals this contract owns (Step-0 verdict + reachability verdict): moon-cluster crawl labyrinth, boundary-start keep-out dip, barrier-pin dwell bound, tightest-moon-0 far-side visit. GUARDRAILS: SC_TUNING byte-identical; WS-1 CRUISE stall detector semantics preserved (DEPART gets its OWN timeout so it cannot false-trip the CRUISE-keyed detector); inc-1 standoff/go-around and 7/5 reachability fixes stay green; regime/UI/station files untouched (sibling A's territory).

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A pure pilot-layer DEPART phase realizes Max's vision: starting at/near a body, the ship first climbs radially away (v/vmax-gated), then orbits the current body until the nose points over its horizon toward the next target, then hands off to TRANSIT — with commit-and-hold discipline (no phase thrash, no blended control laws). Built TDD in pure pilot tests mirroring the SupercruisePilot.align test patterns.
